Questions.content: What is the definition of median used here, and does it need to consider the days as part of the data set?

Answers.content:
The definition of median used here refers to the middle value in a sorted list of numbers. If there is an odd number of observations, the median is the value at the position \((n+1)/2\), where \(n\) is the total number of observations. In this case, since there are 7 days (an odd number), the median will be the value at the 4th position when the data is sorted.

The days themselves are not part of the dataset used to find the median; only the number of cups sold each day is considered. The days could be useful for context or other analyses, but they do not affect the calculation of the median in this specific problem.

The median of a data set is the middle value when the data points are arranged in ascending or descending order. If there is an odd number of data points, the median is indeed the middle value. However, if there is an even number of data points, the median is calculated as the average of the two middle values.

In this case, we have 7 days (an odd number), so the median will be the value in the 4th position when the data is sorted. If it were an even number of days, say 8 days, then the median would be the average of the 4th and 5th values.
